what: STRUCTURAL manifest for the M4 PR 8a Band 4 corpus: what each document is, how many recipe nodes it has, and how many of them fall in the downstream cone of its latency row's parameter edit. Machine-independent and exact — nothing about a box, a build profile or a load average can move these numbers, which is why they live apart from the timings.
timings_live_elsewhere: docs/perf-data/rebuild-latency/ — one file per merge to main, written and committed by ci.yml's `rebuild latency (reporting)` job on a hosted runner. Append-only (a run adds a filename, never edits one), so concurrent merges cannot conflict. m4_pr8_latency.rs diffs its `vs base` columns against the NEWEST entry: on a PR that is main's last hosted measurement, on main it is the previous merge. There is no baseline to refresh and no refresh env var.
why_split: Timings and structure shared one file until 2026-08-17, and the timings rotted it. Three developer-workstation refreshes disagreed by 90-98% on every row (die full: 51661.1 ms -> ~985.9 ms -> 1103.5 ms) with contention ruled out by a verified-quiet re-run, leaving an untested build/environment hypothesis nobody ever captured side by side; the file's own provenance ended up declaring cross-refresh comparison meaningless, and docs/PERF-SCAN-2026-08.md §0 had to label every absolute-millisecond claim in the repo provisional as a result. Splitting along the rot line fixes the cause: the half that cannot rot is pinned here and ASSERTED (a nodes/cone mismatch fails the row), and the half that can is produced by one reproducible box class and accumulated rather than overwritten. The disputed_measurement argument is not resolved retroactively — those three refreshes stay incomparable — it simply cannot recur, because every history entry now records its own build environment.
status: The TIMINGS are REPORTING ONLY — measured, never gated (M4-PLAN F8; PERF-PLAN stays advisory). No CI row fails on a millisecond. The STRUCTURE below is a real assertion: m4_pr8_latency.rs requires the manifest to cover the corpus exactly (no missing rows, no stale keys) and every nodes/cone pair to match what it measures.
maintaining: Hand-maintained. A document that legitimately changes shape moves its nodes/cone here in the same PR, with the reason in the PR body; a new corpus document adds a row; a retired one deletes its row. The row fails loudly either way, so this file cannot silently fall behind the corpus.
